stem: Which of the following hormones is released from the posterior pituitary when plasma osmolality rises?

options.label: A
options.misconception: A sodium-retaining cortical steroid is being substituted for the water-retaining peptide.
options.explanation: Aldosterone acts on principal cells for sodium retention; the osmolality-triggered posterior-pituitary release is ADH.

options.label: B
options.text: Atrial natriuretic peptide from the atria
options.misconception: A volume-overload natriuretic peptide is being treated as the high-osmolality response.
options.explanation: ANP responds to atrial stretch; rising osmolality triggers hypothalamic osmoreceptors to release ADH from the posterior pituitary.

options.label: C
options.misconception: None; vasopressin (ADH) is the posterior-pituitary water-conserving hormone.
options.explanation: Hypothalamic osmoreceptors detect rising plasma osmolality and signal release of vasopressin (ADH) from the posterior pituitary to conserve water.

options.label: D
options.misconception: The neighboring posterior-pituitary peptide is being confused with ADH.
options.explanation: Oxytocin drives uterine contraction and milk ejection; the osmolality-response peptide is ADH.

options.label: E
options.misconception: A renal pressure sensor product is being cast as the hypothalamic osmolality hormone.
options.explanation: Renin responds to reduced renal perfusion; rising osmolality triggers ADH release from the posterior pituitary.

context: Learning objective: name the osmolality-triggered posterior-pituitary hormone. Rising plasma osmolality → hypothalamic osmoreceptors → ADH release.
